Format.name: Format
Format.usage: Legal value: GC-NPD-95 (not in any lookup table). It is highly recommended that this record be the first in the file definition block.

Version.name: Version
Version.usage: Legal values: 2.0  (not in any lookup table). Version 1.0 is now obsolete. It is highly recommended that this record be the second in the file definition block.

Dictionary.name: Dictionary
Dictionary.usage: Legal values: GC-DIC-V2 (see sheet "Dictionary"). GC-DIC-V1 is now obsolete. It is highly recommended that this record  be the third in the file definition block.

TransferID.name: TransferID
TransferID.description: Unique identifier for the data transfer job
TransferID.usage: Consists of: Sender + unique ID-code. A new TransferID must be used each time a data set is changed and retransmitted.

TransferDate.name: TransferDate
TransferDate.usage: Date when the file was generated or last edited. Format DD.MM.YYYY

DTJStatus.name: DTJStatus
DTJStatus.description: Status of the data transfer job
DTJStatus.usage: Legal values: a DTJStatus code from the "LookupValue" sheet.

Sender.name: Sender
Sender.description: Organisation who sends the transfer file
Sender.usage: Typically the laboratory or the operator. Legal values: a  company code from see sheet "LookupValue".

Contact.name: Contact
Contact.usage: Person who creates the transfer file or is responsible for its transmittal.

Recipient.name: Recipient
Recipient.description: Name of organisation to which the transfer file is sent
Recipient.usage: Typically the operator (if sent by a laboratory) or NPD/Petrobank (if sent by the operator). Legal values: a  company code from the sheet "LookupValue". Optional, as only for the sender's record.

Delimiter.name: Delimiter
Delimiter.usage: Legal values: a  delimiter code from the sheet "LookupValue". Mandatory for all character-delimited formats, optional for column-bound format (i.e. column-bound format is the default). New in Version 2.0.

DTJComments.name: DTJComments
DTJComments.description: Comments on an individual data transfer job
DTJComments.usage: Free text comment, e.g. references to earlier transmitted data, any other messages to the recipient. New in Version 2.0.

SiteID.name: SiteID
SiteID.usage: Used as a transfer-file internal sample site identifier. Used to relate samples to their respective sample site when multiple sites are included in a data transfer job.

Country.name: Country
Country.usage: Legal values: Alpha-2 country code (2 characters) as per ISO 3166 . See country codes in the "LookupValue" sheet.

SiteType.name: SiteType
SiteType.usage: Legal values: a  site type code from the sheet "LookupValue".

SiteName.name: SiteName
SiteName.usage: Unique name for the sample site, e.g. well name or name of a geographical area. The format for Norwegian well names is described in the "Provisions"  or in the Web document "Classification of wells and wellbores" . For sites other than wells, standardised geographical area names shall be used where available. The site name UNKNOWN may be used for reference samples, or for surface samples if the coordinates are reported.

DatumName.name: DatumName
DatumName.description: Name of local vertical datum for sample depth values
DatumName.usage: Name of the local datum for depths of all samples reported from this site, for example RKB (rotary kelly bushings), MSL (mean sea level) or SB (sea bed). For outcrop samples use MSL (and negative depth values). UNKNOWN must only be used for "old" data, where the datum cannot be identified, or for reference samples.

DatumElevation.name: DatumElevation
DatumElevation.description: Elevation of local vertical datum for sample depth values
DatumElevation.usage: Elevation of the local datum in metres above mean sea level (m MSL). This elevation may be unknown.

SSLatitude.name: SSLatitude
SSLatitude.usage: Degrees * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds. + for N and – for S. Mandatory for surface samples where the sample site names are not officially registered and the position hence cannot be derived from the sample site name.

SSLongitude.name: SSLongitude
SSLongitude.usage: Degrees * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds. + for E, - for W. Otherwise same rules as for SSLatitude.

PosnDatum.name: PosnDatum
PosnDatum.usage: Name (abbreviated) of geodetic datum (normally ED-50 or WGS-84).

SSComments.name: SSComments
SSComments.description: Comments on an individual sample site.
SSComments.usage: Free text comment, e.g. on use of Logger's vs. driller's depth, depth corrections for cores, mud systems, outcrop location description.

UDepth.name: UDepth
UDepth.description: Depth at top of sampled interval
UDepth.usage: “Depth” is measured depth relative to the local datum of the sample site. Logger's depth is normally used for drill cuttings and driller's depth (core depth) is normally used for cores. For clarity, however, it is highly recommend to explicitly specify the "kind" of depth used, either (for single samples) in the SComments field or (for all samples together) in the SSComments field. Levels above the datum shall be provided as negative values, levels below the datum as positive values in order to comply with the norm of reporting well samples with positive depths. Upper and lower depth shall always be given, even if they are identical (i.e. for spot samples). If a depth is unknown, the keyword UNKNOWN shall be used.

LDepth.name: LDepth
LDepth.description: Depth at bottom of sampled interval

SampleType.name: SampleType
SampleType.description: Code to indicate sample material and associated sampling method
SampleType.usage: Legal values: A sample type code from the "LookupValue" sheet.

LabRefNumber.name: LabRefNumber
LabRefNumber.description: Sample reference number, unique within a given laboratory.
LabRefNumber.usage: One sample may have several LabRefNumbers, e.g. one given by the operator and others given by various laboratories.

OpRefNumber.name: OpRefNumber
OpRefNumber.usage: Sample ID or sample name used by the operator or client, e.g. "DST 1B", "S12345", "Bottle # A98765". Used to relate an analysed sample to sample descriptions appearing elsewhere.

SCompany.name: SCompany
SCompany.usage: Legal values: A company code from the "LookupValue" sheet (if possible) or the official name of the company.

SInstrument.name: SInstrument
SInstrument.description: Type of sampling or drilling equipment

SLithology.name: SLithology
SLithology.description: Short, coded description of the sample's lithology.
SLithology.usage: Legal values: A text string composed of codes from the "Lithology" sheet, using the syntax outlined in the Specification document. Mandatory for rock samples (as the fraction lithology may refer to the sample lithology).

SLithologyFull.name: SLithologyFull
SLithologyFull.description: Description of sample lithology in the sender's format.
SLithologyFull.usage: New in version 2.0. Optional attribute that allows to include the sender's full sample description in addition to the short, coded SLithology.

SComments.name: SComments
SComments.usage: Free text comment, e.g. on sample quality. Mandatory if SampleType is OTH (see Sample Type codes in the "LookupValue" sheet).

SLatitude.name: SLatitude
SLatitude.usage: Degrees * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds. + for N, - for S. Used for surface or outcrop samples where the geographical position is not implicit from the sample site name (as it is in wells). Unnecessary for well samples since the exact position can be calculated from well deviation data.

SLongitude.name: SLongitude
SLongitude.usage: Degrees * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds. + for E, - for W. Same usage as SLatitude.

FractionID.name: FractionID
FractionID.description: Fraction identifier, unique within the transfer file.
FractionID.usage: Used as a transfer-file internal fraction identifier.

FracRefNumber.name: FracRefNumber
FracRefNumber.description: Fraction identifier, unique within the laboratory.
FracRefNumber.usage: Must allow unambiguous tracing of material and data for a given fraction.

FractionType.name: FractionType
FractionType.description: Code to indicate fraction material and preparation method
FractionType.usage: Legal values: A fraction type code from the "LookupValue" sheet.

FLithology.name: FLithology
FLithology.description: Short, coded description of the lithology from which this fraction was derived.
FLithology.usage: Legal values: A text string composed of codes from the "Lithology" sheet, using the syntax outlined in the Specification document. Mandatory for all fractions derived from rock samples. If the whole sample was analysed, the fraction lithology is BULK.

FLithologyFull.name: FLithologyFull
FLithologyFull.description: Description of fraction lithology in the sender's format.
FLithologyFull.usage: Free text, not controlled by a lookup table. New in version 2.0. Allows to include the sender's full fraction description in addition to the short, coded one.

FComments.name: FComments
FComments.usage: Free text comment, e.g. on preparation method, losses, lithology. Mandatory if FractionType = OTH (see Fraction Type dictionary table).

AnalID.name: AnalID
AnalID.usage: Used as a transfer-file internal analysis identifier.

AnalType.name: AnalType
AnalType.usage: Legal values: An analysis type code from the "AnalysisType" sheet.

ADescription.name: ADescription
ADescription.description: Purpose of analysis / type of material analysed (normal sample or reference standard)
ADescription.usage: Legal values: An ADescription code from the "LookupValue" sheet.

ALaboratory.name: ALaboratory
ALaboratory.description: Company name of the laboratory that performed the analysis
ALaboratory.usage: Legal values: A company code from the "LookupValue" sheet (if possible) or the official name of the company/laboratory.

AMethod.name: AMethod
AMethod.usage: Defaults to description in NIGOGA. Mandatory if non-NIGOGA method used.

ADate.name: ADate
ADate.description: Date at which analysis was performed
ADate.usage: Format DD.MM.YYYY. Strongly recommended but not mandatory.

AComments.name: AComments
AComments.usage: Free text comment, e.g. on analytical method, problems. Mandatory if non-NIGOGA method used.

ParamName.name: ParamName
ParamName.usage: Legal values: A parameter name from the "ParameterName" sheet.

ParamValue.name: ParamValue
ParamValue.usage: UOM is defined in the NIGOGA. It is also listed in the Parameter Name dictionary table, except for parameters from GC analyses, where the UOM is implicitely defined through the PeakProperty value, see the LookupValue sheet. For the representation of missing values see the Specification document.

Detector.name: Detector
Detector.usage: Legal values: A detector code from the "LookupValue" sheet. New in version 2.0. Mandatory for GC analyses (i.e. AnalType = GC).

PeakProperty.name: PeakProperty
PeakProperty.usage: Legal values: A peak property code from the "LookupValue" sheet. New in version 2.0. Mandatory for GC analyses (i.e. AnalType = GC).

PopnNum.name: PopnNum
PopnNum.description: Running number of the vitrinite population to be reported
PopnNum.usage: New in version 2.0. Replaces the "PopnNo" parameter of version 1.0. Mandatory for vitrinite reflectance analyses (i.e. AnalType = VR).

PComments.name: PComments
PComments.usage: Free text comment, e.g. on peak interference, contaminants etc. Replaces the "COMMENT" parameter of version 1.0. New in version 2.0.

5.SURFACE: All samples taken from the earth's surface, including outcrop samples, seabed samples (e.g. grab samples) and soft sediment core samples (e.g. gravity core, piston core)
5.WELL: All samples taken from wells or shallow drillholes, where the geographical position normally is officially registered and thus implicit from the borehole name

6.CCOM: Core chip, composite sample (i.e. core chips from a significant depth interval (>5 cm) combined)
6.COCH: Core, chip, small piece with specified depth
6.COFI: Core, chip, from junk basket while fishing
6.SCOM: Sidewall core, composite sample (i.e. material from more than one SWC combined into one sample)
6.SRFC: Surface sediment core, chip, small piece/volume with specified depth

7.GSHO: Gas, sum of headspace and occluded fractions
7.KEXT: Kerogen concentrate prepared from extracted sediment
7.KSED: Kerogen concentrate prepared from unextracted sediment
7.MOIL: Drilling mud, total base oil (or other extracted additive) fraction
7.SDPY: Sediment, pyrolysate (temperature-programmed), from unextracted sediment (corresponding to Rock-Eval S2 peak)
7.SDTE: Thermal extract from unextracted sediment (corresponding to Rock-Eval S1 peak)
7.SLKO: Kerogen slide, oxidised kerogen (sieved or total)

8.A: Analysis of "normal" samples (i.e. Not reference samples
8.S: Control analysis of reference ( standard) samples

9.123: Mass spectrometer, tuned to m/z 123 (tetracyclic terpanes)
9.163: Mass spectrometer, tuned to m/z 163 (tetracyclic terpanes)
9.177: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 177(.1643) (terpanes, particularly demethylated hopanes)
9.191: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 191(.1800) (tri- and tetracyclic diterpanes, pentacyclic triterpanes)
9.205: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 205(.1956) (pentacyclic hopane-type triterpanes, particularly methylhopanes and C31)
9.217: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 217(.1956) (regular and rearranged steranes) or m/z 217.0891 (for benzo-carbazoles)
9.218: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 218(.2035) (regular and rearranged steranes, mainly bb-steranes)
9.219: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 219(.1174) (retene (base peak)) or m/z 219.2113 (pentacyclic hopane-type triterpanes)
9.231: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 231(.1174) (triaromatic steroids) or m/z 231.2113 (4-methylsteranes)
9.253: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 253(.1956) (monoaromatic steroids)
9.257: Mass spectrometer, tuned to m/z 257 (rearranged sterenes)
9.259: Mass spectrometer tuned to m/z 259(.2426) (rearranged steranes = diasteranes)
9.267: Mass spectrometer, tuned to m/z 267 (C-ring aromatised steroids)
9.358->217: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 358.3599 -> 217.1956 (C26 steranes)
9.370->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 370.3608 -> 191.1800 (C27 terpanes)
9.372->217: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 372.3756 -> 217.1956 (C27 steranes)
9.384->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 384.3757 -> 191.1800 (C28 terpanes)
9.386->217: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 386.3913 -> 217.1956 (C28 steranes)
9.398->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 398.3914 -> 191.1800 (C29-terpanes)
9.400->217: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 400.4069 -> 217.1956 (C29 steranes)
9.412->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 412.4069 -> 191.1800 (C30 terpanes)
9.414->217: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 414.4226 -> 217.1956 (C30 steranes)
9.426->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 426.4226 -> 191.1800 (C31 terpanes)
9.440->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 440.4382 -> 191.1800 (C32 terpanes)
9.454->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 454.4539 -> 191.1800 (C33 terpanes)
9.468->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 468.4695 -> 191.1800 (C34 terpanes)
9.482->191: Mass spectrometer tuned to the determination of the metastable transition m/z 482.4852 -> 191.1800 (C35 terpanes)
9.DELTA13C: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometer, tuned to the determination of d13C
9.DELTA18O: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometer, tuned to the determination of d18O
9.DELTA2H: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometer, tuned to the determination of d2H
9.DELTA34S: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometer, tuned to the determination of d34S

10.AREA: Area of peak in chromatogram (see NIGOGA).
10.CNCAREA: Concentration of measured component based on peak area.
10.CNCHEIGHT: Concentration of measured component based on peak height.
10.HEIGHT: Height of peak in chromatogram (see NIGOGA).
10.NORMAREA: Normalised value of measured component based on peak area: Percent of sum of peak areas.
10.NORMHEIGHT: Normalised value of measured component based on peak height: Percent of sum of peak heights.
10.UNKNOWN: To be used only for reporting of "old" data, where PeakProperty cannot be derived from the documentation. New in version 2.0.

11.UNKNOWN: SiteName only used for geochemical standard samples.

RE.comment: TOC analysis and bulk-flow pyrolysis-FID (Rock-Eval). Raw data (S1, S2, Tmax etc.) and derived data (PP, PI, HI, OI etc.).

VR.comment: Vitrinite reflectance analysis and (optionally) visual description of liptinite fluorescence in polished section. Raw data (reflectances of individual points) and derived data (mean reflectance etc.).

VK.comment: Visual kerogen description (on kerogen slide in transmitted light), spore color determination

MGA.comment: Maceral group analysis (on polished section in reflected light)

BULKHC.comment: Extraction/separation of EOM or fluid (oil), including: solvent extraction, asphaltene precipitation and TLC-FID (Iatroscan) analysis

GC.comment: Gas chromatography and all "hyphenated" methods like PY-GC, GC-MS, GC-IRMS, isotope analysis of single compounds after preparative GC, etc.

PHYS.comment: Physical analysis of fluid (density, percentage of C15+ fraction etc.).

ISOT.comment: Stable isotope analysis of whole oil or EOM, oil or EOM fractions, kerogen. Isotope analysis of specific compounds (by GC-IRMS or after isolation by preparative GC) belongs to GC, with the isotope ratio name as Detector value and ISOTRATIO as PeakProperty.

ELEMENT.comment: Elemental analysis of whole oil or EOM, oil or EOM fractions, kerogen. New in version 2.0. Not described in NIGOGA.

253.usage: Use this variable if tricyclic peak is broad or poorly resolved.

263.usage: tricyclic peak may be double peak

S0.name: S0
S0.usage: Reported only if Rock-Eval III/OSA, not in NIGOGA. TOC can be determined using Rock-Eval or carbon analyzer (to be stated in Acomments)

TOC.name: TOC
TOC.remarks: Total organic carbon content of rock (fraction) or kerogen isolate
TOC.usage: TOC can be determined using Rock-Eval or carbon analyzer (to be stated in Acomments).

TMAX.name: TMAX
TMAX.remarks: Temperature at maximum of S2 peak

PopnMean.name: PopnMean
PopnMean.description: Mean of random reflectance in oil for the reported vitrinite population (Rm)

PopnRead.name: PopnRead
PopnRead.description: Number of readings of the reported vitrinite population

PopnLRange.name: PopnLRange
PopnLRange.description: Lower Ro limit of the reported vitrinite population

PopnURange.name: PopnURange
PopnURange.description: Upper Ro limit of the reported vitrinite population

PopnStdev.name: PopnStdev
PopnStdev.description: Standard deviation of Rm of the reported vitrinite population

VRReliability.name: VRReliability
VRReliability.description: Remarks on data reliability (for each phytoclast population)

VRQuality.name: VRQuality
VRQuality.description: Remarks on nature and quality of the phytoclasts (for each population)

Fcol.name: Fcol
Fcol.description: Fluorescence colour(s) of the liptinite population(s) present in the polished section.
Fcol.usage: Free text or codes with explanation. Not necessary to give separate values for each population.

Roil.name: Roil
Roil.usage: Text string containing all individual values separated by the character used as Delimiter in the transfer file.

FA.name: FA
FA.usage: All percentages must be normalised to 100%. Traces may be reported as e.g. 0.1 or mentioned in a comment.

SCI.name: SCI
SCI.usage: Free text. Must be reported for each palynomorph polulation.

VKAbundance.name: VKAbundance
VKAbundance.description: Comments on the relative abundances of palynomorph populations selected for SCI determination.

SCIQuality.name: SCIQuality
SCIQuality.description: Comments on quality and reliability of SCI values for each palynomorph population selected for SCI determination.

MIN.name: MIN
MIN.usage: At present no further fields are defined (e.g. for individual macerals).

TOCEOM.name: TOCEOM
TOCEOM.description: TOC content of fraction used for extraction

SATTOC.name: SATTOC

AROTOC.name: AROTOC
AROTOC.usage: If NOT from TLC-FID (calibr., as described in the NIGOGA), then describe the data source (analysis type) in Acomments or PComments.

HCNHC.name: HCNHC

C6toC14_WithUCM.name: C6toC14_WithUCM

C15plus_NoUCM.name: C15plus_NoUCM

rules.text: If no column-bound format is used, Delimiter is a mandatory attribute.  Or the other way round: If Delimiter IS "COLUMN" OR Data_Transfer_Job.Delimiter Is Missing Then use column-bound format.
rules.comment: Attribute of Data Transfer Job. Probably no check possible, as this would have to be derived from the format itself, e.g. if the column range definitions are missing or if a comma, semicolon etc. is found in the data blocks...

rules.text: If SiteName not found in NPD's wellbore list Then SSLatitude Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Sample Site. Must be present if not an officially registered well. Hans/Oddbjørn: How to check this against NPD's list? And what with e.g. Danish and British wells? Can't probably be checked technically, but the person creating the file should be aware of this rule.

rules.text: If SiteName not found in NPD's wellbore list Then SSLongitude Is Mandatory
If SampleType = ("CCOM" Or "COCH" Or "COFI" Or "COPL" Or "COSP" Or "DC" Or "DCG" Or "DCOM" Or "OC" Or "SWC" Or "SCOM" Or "SRFC") Then SLithology Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Sample. All these sample types refer to rock samples, and the rock type (lithology) must be described.

rules.text: If SampleType = "OTH" Then SComments Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Sample. The sample type must be described in the SComments field if the sample type is "OTH"(er).

rules.text: If SampleType = ("CCOM" Or "COCH" Or "COFI" Or "COPL" Or "COSP" Or "DC" Or "DCG" Or "DCOM" Or "OC" Or "SWC" Or "SCOM" Or "SRFC")  Then FLithology Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Fraction. "BULK" is a legal FLithology (this means that the fraction has the same lithology as the whole sample).

rules.text: If FractionType = "OTH" Then FComments Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Fraction. The fraction must be described in the FComments field if the fraction type is "OTH"(er).

rules.text: If non-NIGOGA method used Then AMethod Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Analysis. Impossible to check as there is no code for recognition of method details (i.e. NIGOGA vs. non-NIGOGA).

rules.text: If non-NIGOGA method used Then AComment Is Mandatory
rules.comment: Attribute of Analysis. Impossible to check as there is no code for recognition of method details (i.e. NIGOGA vs. non-NIGOGA).

rules.text: If Left(AnalType,2) = "GC" Then Detector Is Mandatory
If Left(AnalType,2) = "GC" Then PeakProperty Is Mandatory
If ADescription = "S" (i.e. if it's a reference / standard sample) Then SiteName Can Be "UNKNOWN" (otherwise this value is illegal)
